```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 17_correlation_your_turn_causation
title: Your turn
questions:
  - id: reverse_and_third
    type: free-response
    prompt: >
      Suppose a survey finds that teenagers who spend more time on social
      media report lower well-being. It's tempting to conclude that social
      media makes teenagers unhappy. Come up with two other explanations: one
      where the causation runs the other way, and one where a third variable
      is behind both.
    answerLabel: Example answer
    answer: >
      The other way around: teenagers who are already unhappy might spend more
      time on social media, perhaps looking for distraction or company. A
      third variable: teenagers with less going on in their lives, or with
      less parental supervision, might both spend more time online and feel
      worse, without either one causing the other.
    explanation: >
      There are plenty of other possibilities. The point is that the
      correlation by itself can't tell them apart.
```
